title: Family Lawyer Salary: Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a family lawyer salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes award rates, tax, and superannuation.
salarySummary: Under the Legal Services Award, a family lawyer at Level 5 (law graduate) earns a minimum of $33.99 per hour, or about $67,200 annually for a 38-hour week before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a family lawyer under the Legal Services Award?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the Legal Services Award sets minimum hourly rates for legal employees. A family lawyer classified as a Law Graduate (Level 5) earns $33.99 per hour, while a Law Clerk (Level 6) earns $36.03 per hour. These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees working a 38-hour week. Many experienced family lawyers earn above these award minimums.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a family lawyer's pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Legal Services Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a family lawyer at Level 5, the casual rate is $42.49 per hour ($33.99 × 1.25). This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casuals do not receive. The loading is applied to the base rate, so you should never enter a rate that already includes casual loading when using a calculator.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on a family lawyer's salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a family lawyer earning $67,200 per year, that means an extra $8,064 in super contributions, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional payment your employer makes into a super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Family Lawyer Salary

If you are a family lawyer or considering a career in family law, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary is essential for comparing job offers, negotiating pay, or planning your finances. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week and 52-week year to give you a clear picture of your potential earnings, including tax and superannuation. We draw on official sources such as the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Fair Work Commission, and the Australian Taxation Office to ensure accuracy.

### The 38-Hour Week and 52-Week Year

Australia’s standard full-time work week is 38 hours, as defined by the National Employment Standards. When converting an hourly rate to an annual salary, the formula is simple:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a family lawyer earning $33.99 per hour (the minimum for a Law Graduate under the Legal Services Award), the calculation is:

$33.99 × 38 × 52 = $67,200.24 per year

If you are paid a salary instead of an hourly rate, you can reverse the formula to find your equivalent hourly rate: divide your annual salary by 2,000 (38 × 52 is approximately 1,976, but many use 2,000 for simplicity).

### The Fortnight View

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same example:

Weekly pay: $33.99 × 38 = $1,291.62
Fortnightly pay: $1,291.62 × 2 = $2,583.24

This can help you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly or annual figures.

## Family Lawyer Salary Under the Legal Services Award

The [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman show that the Legal Services Award (MA000116) covers family lawyers and other legal employees. From 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rates for key classifications are:

- Legal clerical and administrative employee, Level 5: $33.99 per hour
- Law graduate, Level 5: $33.99 per hour
- Law clerk, Level 6: $36.03 per hour

These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate for a Level 5 family lawyer $42.49 per hour. You can find the full award rates in the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guide and the Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database.

Note that these are minimum rates. Many family lawyers with experience or in private practice earn significantly more. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 annually. A family lawyer’s salary can vary based on location, firm size, and specialisation.

## Tax and Superannuation

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your take-home pay after tax and the super your employer pays on top.

### Income Tax (2026–27)

The resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a family lawyer earning $67,200, the tax estimate is:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 (up to $45,000): $4,020
- Tax on remaining $22,200 (up to $67,200): $6,660
- Total tax: $10,680
- Medicare levy: $1,344
- Total deductions: $12,024
- Take-home pay: approximately $55,176 per year

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed calculation.

### Superannuation

Your employer must pay superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For a $67,200 salary, that’s an extra $8,064 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution to your super fund. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Casual Loading and Other Considerations

If you work as a casual family lawyer, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading. When using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, enter the base rate without the loading, then check the casual loading box. For example, if your base rate is $33.99, the tool will add $8.50 to give a casual rate of $42.49. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

## Conclusion

Converting your family lawyer salary from hourly to annual gives you a clear picture of your earnings. Remember the 38-hour week, 52-week year formula, and factor in tax and super. For the most accurate rates, always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides and the Fair Work Commission’s database. Whether you are negotiating a new role or planning your budget, understanding these numbers puts you in control.

For more tools, see our [reference tables](/data) and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.
